    45→class LoRAFinetuneRecipeDistributed(FTRecipeInterface):
    46→    """
    47→    Distributed LoRA finetuning recipe for dense transformer-based LLMs such as Llama2. This recipe supports
    48→    distributed training and can be run on a single node (1 to 8 GPUs).
    49→
    50→    Features:
    51→        - FSDP. Supported using PyTorch's FSDP APIs. CPU offload of parameters, gradients, and optimizer states
    52→            is supported via ``fsdp_cpu_offload``. Resharding of parameters after the forward pass is
    53→            done by default (corresponding to FULL_SHARD sharding strategy), but can be disabled by setting the config
    54→            ``fsdp_reshard_after_forward`` to False (this corresponds to SHARD_GRAD_OP sharding strategy).
    55→            DDP is currently not supported. Training on CPU is not supported.
    56→
    57→        - Activation Checkpointing. This can be controlled using the ``enable_activation_checkpointing``
    58→            flag. Activation checkpointing helps reduce the memory footprint since we no longer keep
    59→            activations in memory and instead recompute them during the backward pass. This is especially
    60→            helpful for larger batch sizes when you're memory constrained. But these savings in memory
    61→            come at the cost of training performance. In most cases training can slow-down quite a bit as
    62→            a result of this activation recomputation.
    63→
    64→        - Activation Offloading. This can be controlled using the ``enable_activation_offloading``
    65→            flag. Activation offloading is a technique similar to activations checkpointing that helps
    66→            reduce the memory footprint to prevent OOMs on CUDA and enable bigger batches. Where activations
    67→            checkpointing drops the activation in the forward to recompute it later in the backward,
    68→            activations offloading will drop the activation in the forward to the CPU and bring it
    69→            back during the backward pass. As always, there is a tradeoff--these savings in memory can
    70→            come at the cost of training performance and CPU resources. To recover some runtime cost,
    71→            we've added an option to enable offloading on a different stream to permit overlapping with
    72→            the computation. This option is currently only available on PyTorch 2.5.0 or later and will be
    73→            enabled by default if an acceptable torch version is found. Activation offloading can be used in
    74→            conjunction with activation checkpointing.
    75→
    76→        - Precision. Full fp32 and bf16 training are supported. Precision is controlled using the ``dtype``
    77→            flag. When ``dtype=bf16``, all activations, gradients and optimizer states are in bfloat16. In
    78→            most cases this should halve the memory footprint of full precision (fp32) training, without
    79→            loss in model quality (will depend on the model, training data and other settings). For
    80→            GPUs which do not support bfloat16, we fall back to fp32. Mixed precision training and fp16
    81→            precision are currently not supported.
    82→
    83→        - Gradient Accumulation. You can simulate larger batch sizes by accumulating gradients. This is
    84→            controlled using the ``gradient_accumulation_steps`` flag.
    85→
    86→                Total Batch Size = batch_size * number of GPUs * gradient accumulation steps.
    87→
    88→            For example: with batch_size=1, nproc_per_node=2 and gradient_accumulation_steps=32 we get a
    89→            total batch size of 64.
    90→
    91→            Gradient accumulation is especially useful when you are memory constrained. In this case,
    92→            accumulating gradients might give you better training speed than enabling activation
    93→            checkpointing.
    94→
    95→        - Checkpointing. Model weights are checkpointed both at the end of each epoch and at the end of
    96→            training. Currently we checkpoint both the adapter weights (trainable params only) and the
    97→            complete merged weights (adapter weights added back to the base model). For more details
    98→            please take a look at our LoRA tutorial
    99→            (https://pytorch.org/torchtune/main/tutorials/lora_finetune.html).
   100→
   101→            Optimizer State and recipe state (seed, total_epochs, number of epochs run etc) are
   102→            only saved at the end of a given epoch and used in case of resuming training. Resuming
   103→            training is controlled by the ``resume_from_checkpoint`` flag. Mid-epoch checkpointing is
   104→            currently not supported.
   105→
   106→            For more details on the checkpointer, please take a look at
   107→            our checkpointer deepdive (https://pytorch.org/torchtune/main/tutorials/checkpointer.html).
   108→
   109→        - Logging. Terminal, Disk, WandB and TensorBoard are all supported.
   110→
   111→        - Gradient Clipping. Gradient clipping is supported using the ``clip_grad_norm`` flag. By default,
   112→            ``clip_grad_norm`` is set to ``None``. If you only want to log the grad norm, you can set
   113→            ``clip_grad_norm='inf'``.
   114→
   115→    For a full list of example configs for this recipe, run ``tune ls`` on the command line. Each config
   116→    has example commands for how to kick-off training.
   117→

   119→        cfg (DictConfig): OmegaConf object parsed from yaml file

   122→        ValueError: If ``dtype`` is set to fp16.
   123→        ValueError: If world_size is 1

   635→    def save_checkpoint(
   636→        self,
   637→        epoch: int,
   638→    ) -> None:
   639→        """
   640→        Checkpoint the state of the recipe. The constructed checkpoint state dict
   641→        contains the following information:
   642→        - Merged weights with key MODEL_KEY
   643→        - Adapter weights with key ADAPTER_KEY
   644→        - Relevant recipe state if training is not complete
   645→        - If the `self._save_adapter_weights_only` option is True, the checkpointer will save only the adapter weights
   646→
   647→        Checkpointer will save the merged weights, adapter weights and recipe state in
   648→        different checkpoint files. To correctly resume from training, the adapter weights
   649→        and recipe state must be provided along with the base model weights.
   650→        """
   651→        # final dict passed onto the checkpointer
   652→        checkpoint_dict = {}
   653→
   654→        intermediate_checkpoint = epoch + 1 < self.total_epochs
   655→
   656→        utils.log_rank_zero(
   657→            log,
   658→            "Saving checkpoint. This may take some time. Retrieving full model state dict...",
   659→        )
   660→        start = time.perf_counter()
   661→
   662→        # To prevent GPU memory from spiking during checkpoint save,
   663→        # we consolidate the full model and optim state dicts on CPU for rank 0
   664→        state_dict = self._model.state_dict()
   665→        if self._save_adapter_weights_only:
   666→            state_dict = get_adapter_state_dict(state_dict, device=None)
   667→
   668→        cpu_state_dict = training.gather_cpu_state_dict(
   669→            state_dict,
   670→            self._is_rank_zero,
   671→            device=self._device,
   672→        )
   673→        utils.log_rank_zero(
   674→            log,
   675→            f"Getting full model state dict took {time.perf_counter() - start:.2f} secs",
   676→        )
   677→
   678→        if intermediate_checkpoint:
   679→            utils.log_rank_zero(log, "Retrieving optimizer state dict...")
   680→            opt_state_dict = training.get_full_optimizer_state_dict(
   681→                self._optimizer,
   682→                self._is_rank_zero,
   683→                device=self._device,
   684→            )
   685→            utils.log_rank_zero(
   686→                log,
   687→                f"Getting optimizer state dict took {time.perf_counter() - start:.2f} secs",
   688→            )
   689→        else:
   690→            opt_state_dict = None
   691→
   692→        # Now that we have the model and opt state dict, create the actual checkpoint dict
   693→        # to be sent to the checkpointer and ultimately written to file
   694→        if self._is_rank_zero:
   695→            start = time.perf_counter()
   696→
   697→            if self._save_adapter_weights_only:
   698→                adapter_state_dict = cpu_state_dict
   699→            else:
   700→                # Filter out the adapter keys and weights from the model state dict. These will
   701→                # be saved separately
   702→                adapter_state_dict = get_adapter_state_dict(cpu_state_dict)
   703→
   704→                # merge the adapter weights and base weights to create the model checkpoint
   705→                merged_state_dict = get_merged_lora_ckpt(
   706→                    cpu_state_dict,
   707→                    rank=self._lora_rank,
   708→                    alpha=self._lora_alpha,
   709→                )
   710→                checkpoint_dict.update({training.MODEL_KEY: merged_state_dict})
   711→            checkpoint_dict.update({training.ADAPTER_KEY: adapter_state_dict})
   712→
   713→            # if training is in-progress, checkpoint the optimizer state and recipe state
   714→            # as well.
   715→            if intermediate_checkpoint:
   716→                checkpoint_dict.update(
   717→                    {
   718→                        training.OPT_KEY: opt_state_dict,
   719→                        training.SEED_KEY: self.seed,
   720→                        training.EPOCHS_KEY: self.epochs_run,
   721→                        training.TOTAL_EPOCHS_KEY: self.total_epochs,
   722→                        training.MAX_STEPS_KEY: self.max_steps_per_epoch,
   723→                    }
   724→                )
   725→
   726→            adapter_config = {
   727→                "r": self._lora_rank,
   728→                "lora_alpha": self._lora_alpha,
   729→                "target_modules": get_lora_module_names(
   730→                    self._lora_attn_modules,
   731→                    self._apply_lora_to_mlp,
   732→                    self._apply_lora_to_output,
   733→                ),
   734→                "peft_type": "LORA",
   735→            }
   736→            checkpoint_dict.update({training.ADAPTER_CONFIG: adapter_config})
   737→            self._checkpointer.save_checkpoint(
   738→                checkpoint_dict,
   739→                epoch=epoch,
   740→                intermediate_checkpoint=intermediate_checkpoint,
   741→                adapter_only=self._save_adapter_weights_only,
   742→            )
   743→            log.info(f"Saving checkpoint took {time.perf_counter() - start:.2f} secs")
   744→
   745→        torch.distributed.barrier()

   747→    def train(self) -> None:
   748→        """
   749→        The core training loop.
   750→        """
   751→        # clean up before training begins
   752→        training.cleanup_before_training()
   753→
   754→        world_size, rank = training.get_world_size_and_rank()
   755→
   756→        # zero out the gradients before starting training
   757→        self._optimizer.zero_grad()
   758→
   759→        # Initialize tokens count and running loss (for grad accumulation)
   760→        t0 = time.perf_counter()
   761→        running_loss = 0
   762→        num_tokens = 0
   763→
   764→        self._profiler.start()
   765→        # self.epochs_run should be non-zero when we're resuming from a checkpoint
   766→        for curr_epoch in range(self.epochs_run, self.total_epochs):
   767→
   768→            # Update the sampler to ensure data is correctly shuffled across epochs
   769→            # in case shuffle is True
   770→            self._sampler.set_epoch(curr_epoch)
   771→
   772→            pbar = tqdm(total=self._steps_per_epoch, disable=not (rank == 0))
   773→            for idx, batch in enumerate(self._dataloader):
   774→                if (
   775→                    self.max_steps_per_epoch is not None
   776→                    and (idx // self._gradient_accumulation_steps)
   777→                    == self.max_steps_per_epoch
   778→                ):
   779→                    break
   780→
   781→                # Start tracking CUDA memory for active steps for just the first epoch
   782→                if (
   783→                    self._is_rank_zero
   784→                    and curr_epoch == 0
   785→                    and self.profiler_profile_memory
   786→                    and idx == self.profiler_wait_steps + self.profiler_warmup_steps
   787→                ):
   788→                    torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()
   789→
   790→                utils.batch_to_device(batch, self._device)
   791→
   792→                # Calculate the number of unmasked tokens in the current batch
   793→                # and increment the total number of tokens seen in the step
   794→                current_num_tokens = (
   795→                    batch["labels"] != self._loss_fn.ignore_index
   796→                ).sum()
   797→                num_tokens += current_num_tokens
   798→
   799→                # Shape [b, s], needed for the loss not the model
   800→                labels = batch.pop("labels")
   801→
   802→                with self.activations_handling_ctx:
   803→                    logits = self._model(**batch)
   804→
   805→                # Shift labels to compute loss
   806→                # equivalent to doing labels[..., 1:] and logits[..., :-1, :]
   807→                # But this way we dont need to slice the logits. We just add an ignore index to labels.
   808→                labels = torch.hstack(
   809→                    (labels[..., 1:], self.ignore_labels_cache[: labels.shape[0]])
   810→                )
   811→                if not isinstance(logits, list):
   812→                    labels = labels.reshape(-1)
   813→                    logits = logits.reshape(-1, logits.size(-1))
   814→
   815→                # Compute loss
   816→                # Loss is normalized by default so we multiply by the number of tokens
   817→                # This way we can normalize by the total number of tokens if we're accumulating gradients
   818→                current_loss = self._loss_fn(logits, labels) * current_num_tokens
   819→
   820→                # free logits otherwise it peaks backward memory
   821→                del logits
   822→
   823→                running_loss += current_loss
   824→                current_loss.backward()
   825→
   826→                # Step with optimizer
   827→                if (idx + 1) % self._gradient_accumulation_steps == 0:
   828→                    # Get total number of tokens across all ranks to normalize gradients
   829→                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(num_tokens)
   830→                    # This will ensure that the logged loss matches what we're optimizing
   831→                    torch.distributed.all_reduce(running_loss)
   832→                    # Manually scale the gradients from unnormalized loss by total # of tokens
   833→                    training.scale_grads(self._model, 1 / num_tokens)
   834→                    if self._clip_grad_norm is not None:
   835→                        grad_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
   836→                            self._model.parameters(),
   837→                            max_norm=float(self._clip_grad_norm),
   838→                        )
   839→                    self._optimizer.step()
   840→                    self._optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
   841→                    self._lr_scheduler.step()
   842→
   843→                    # Update the number of steps when the weights are updated
   844→                    self.global_step += 1
   845→
   846→                    loss_to_log = running_loss.item() / num_tokens
   847→                    pbar.update(1)
   848→                    pbar.set_description(
   849→                        f"{curr_epoch + 1}|{self.global_step}|Loss: {loss_to_log}"
   850→                    )
   851→
   852→                    # Log per-step metrics
   853→                    if (
   854→                        self.global_step % self._log_every_n_steps == 0
   855→                        and self._is_rank_zero
   856→                    ):
   857→                        time_per_step = time.perf_counter() - t0
   858→                        log_dict = {
   859→                            "loss": loss_to_log,
   860→                            "lr": self._optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"],
   861→                            "tokens_per_second_per_gpu": num_tokens
   862→                            / (time_per_step * world_size),
   863→                        }
   864→                        if self._log_peak_memory_stats:
   865→                            log_dict.update(
   866→                                training.get_memory_stats(device=self._device)
   867→                            )
   868→
   869→                        if self._clip_grad_norm is not None:
   870→                            log_dict.update({"grad_norm": grad_norm})
   871→                        self._metric_logger.log_dict(
   872→                            log_dict,
   873→                            step=self.global_step,
   874→                        )
   875→
   876→                    # Reset running stats for the next step
   877→                    running_loss = 0
   878→                    num_tokens = 0
   879→                    t0 = time.perf_counter()
   880→
   881→                    # Stop tracking CUDA memory now that active steps are complete
   882→                    if (
   883→                        self._is_rank_zero
   884→                        and curr_epoch == 0
   885→                        and self.profiler_profile_memory
   886→                        and idx
   887→                        == self.profiler_wait_steps
   888→                        + self.profiler_warmup_steps
   889→                        + self.profiler_active_steps
   890→                    ):
   891→                        torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(enabled=None)
   892→
   893→                    # Step profiler
   894→                    # Note that this is called within gradient accumulation block, hence
   895→                    # will include multiple forward / backward passes if gradient accumulation > 1
   896→                    self._profiler.step()
   897→
   898→            self.epochs_run += 1
   899→            self.save_checkpoint(epoch=curr_epoch)
   900→
   901→        self._profiler.stop()

    20→class DoRALinear(nn.Module, AdapterModule):
    21→    """DoRA linear layer as introduced in
    22→    `DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models <https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09353>`_.
    23→
    24→    DoRA (Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation) fine-tunes a layer by decomposing the pre-trained weights
    25→    into two components: magnitude and direction. The magnitude component is a learnable scalar vector
    26→    that scales each output channel, while the direction component, modified via LoRA, adjusts the orientation
    27→    of weights. By scaling the LoRA update component :math:`BAx` with the `magnitude` vector, DoRA allows the model
    28→    to apply distinct scaling adjustments across different output dimensions.
    29→
    30→    Args:
    31→        in_dim (int): input dimension
    32→        out_dim (int): output dimension
    33→        rank (int): rank of the low-rank approximation
    34→        alpha (float): scaling factor for the low-rank approximation
    35→        dropout (float): dropout probability. Default: 0.0
    36→        use_bias (bool): whether to include bias in the original linear layer.
    37→            Default: False
    38→        quantize_base (bool): Whether to quantize base linear weight or not.
    39→            Default: False
    40→        **quantization_kwargs: Keyword arguments to pass to `to_nf4` when quantizing the base linear weight.
    41→            Examples of valid arguments are `block_size` and `scaler_block_size`, which control the granularity of
    42→            weight quantization and scaler quantization respectively. This is only used if `quantize_base` is True.
    43→            Default None
    44→
    45→    Raises:
    46→        ValueError: If ``quantize_base`` is False, but quantization kwargs are provided.
    47→
    48→    """
    49→
    50→    def __init__(
    51→        self,
    52→        in_dim: int,
    53→        out_dim: int,
    54→        rank: int,
    55→        alpha: float,
    56→        dropout: float = 0.0,
    57→        use_bias: bool = False,
    58→        quantize_base: bool = False,
    59→        **quantization_kwargs,
    60→    ):
    61→        super().__init__()
    62→        self.in_dim = in_dim
    63→        self.out_dim = out_dim
    64→        self.scaling = alpha / rank
    65→        self.use_bias = use_bias
    66→        self._quantize_base = quantize_base
    67→
    68→        if not self._quantize_base and any([v for v in quantization_kwargs.values()]):
    69→            raise ValueError(
    70→                f"``quantize_base`` is False, but received the following quantization arguments: {quantization_kwargs}"
    71→            )
    72→
    73→        # Setup weight and bias
    74→        linear = nn.Linear(in_features=in_dim, out_features=out_dim, bias=self.use_bias)
    75→        weight = (
    76→            linear.weight
    77→            if not self._quantize_base
    78→            else to_nf4(linear.weight, **quantization_kwargs)
    79→        )

    83→        # this can be used in DPO for treating the dora adapters as the policy model
    84→        # and disabling it to treat the base model as the reference model
    85→        self.disabled = False

    88→            "bias", nn.Parameter(bias) if bias is not None else None

    92→        self.lora_b = nn.Linear(in_features=rank, out_features=out_dim, bias=False)

    96→    def initialize_parameters(self):

    98→        # https://github.com/microsoft/LoRA/blob/4c0333854cb905966f8cc4e9a74068c1e507c7b7/loralib/layers.py#L119
    99→        _lora_a_init_params(self.lora_a)
   100→        _lora_b_init_params(self.lora_b)
   101→
   102→    @torch.no_grad()
   103→    def initialize_dora_magnitude(self):
   104→        """
   105→        DoRA initializes the magnitude vector such that its outputs are initially
   106→        identical to standard LoRA's outputs.
   107→        """
   108→        base_weight = self.weight.to(self.lora_a.weight.dtype)
   109→        lora_weight = self.lora_b.weight @ self.lora_a.weight
   110→        weight_norm = self._get_weight_norm(base_weight, lora_weight)
   111→        self.magnitude.copy_(weight_norm)
   112→
   113→    def _get_weight_norm(self, weight, lora_weight):
   114→        weight = weight + self.scaling * lora_weight
   115→        weight_norm = torch.linalg.norm(weight, dim=1).to(weight.dtype)
   116→        return weight_norm
   117→
   118→    def adapter_params(self) -> List[str]:
   119→        """
   120→        Return lora_a.weight and lora_b.weight as adapter params.
   121→        If bias is enabled, also return lora_a.bias and lora_b.bias.
   122→        """
   123→        adapter_params = ["lora_a.weight", "lora_b.weight", "magnitude"]
   124→        return adapter_params
   125→
   126→    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
   127→        """
   128→        Args:
   129→            x (torch.Tensor): input tensor with shape ``(..., in_dim)``
   130→
   131→        Returns:
   132→            Tensor: output tensor with shape ``(..., out_dim)``
   133→        """
   134→        if self._quantize_base:
   135→            base_out = linear_nf4(input=x, weight=self.weight)
   136→            if self.use_bias:
   137→                base_out = base_out + self.bias
   138→        else:
   139→            base_out = F.linear(x, self.weight, self.bias)
   140→        if self.disabled:
   141→            return base_out
   142→
   143→        x = self.dropout(x)
   144→
   145→        lora_out = self.lora_b(self.lora_a(x))
   146→        # Can't use raw matmul since FSDP hooks are attached to __call__
   147→        # Instead follow the approach in https://github.com/huggingface/peft/pull/1806
   148→        x_eye = torch.eye(
   149→            self.lora_a.weight.shape[1], device=self.lora_a.weight.device, dtype=x.dtype
   150→        )
   151→        lora_weight = self.lora_b(self.lora_a(x_eye)).T
   152→        magnitude = self.magnitude
   153→        weight = self.weight.to(x.dtype)
   154→        weight_norm = self._get_weight_norm(weight, lora_weight.detach())
   155→        weight_norm = weight_norm.detach()
   156→        mag_norm_scale = (magnitude / weight_norm).view(1, -1)
   157→
   158→        dora_out = (
   159→            mag_norm_scale - 1
   160→        ) * base_out + mag_norm_scale * lora_out * self.scaling
   161→
   162→        return dora_out + base_out

   112→def get_adapter_state_dict(
   113→    state_dict: Dict[str, Any], device: Optional[str] = "cpu"
   114→) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   115→    """
   116→    Return the subset of the full state_dict from a model that correspond to an adapter.
   117→    Assumes that "lora" and "magnitude" are unique names for adapter parameters, and
   118→    that the state_dict is not sharded. All returned parameters are moved to CPU.
   119→
   120→    Args:
   121→        state_dict (Dict[str, Any]): Full model state dict.
   122→        device (Optional[str]): device to move adapter parameters to. Default: 'cpu'
   123→
   124→    Returns:
   125→        Dict[str, Any]: the subset of model's state dict containing
   126→        only adapter parameters.
   127→
   128→    """
   129→    adapter_key_filter = lambda x: "lora" in x or "magnitude" in x
   130→    return {k: v.to(device) for k, v in state_dict.items() if adapter_key_filter(k)}

   133→def _get_lora_modules(state_dict: Dict[str, Any]) -> Set[str]:
   134→    """
   135→    Get the keys from a state dict that correspond to LoRALinear modules.
   136→
   137→    For example, if state_dict is the state dict of model and model.x.y.z is a
   138→    LoRALinear, this method will return "model.x.y.z", not
   139→    "model.x.y.z.lora_a.weight" or "model.x.y.z.lora_b.weight".
   140→
   141→    Args:
   142→        state_dict (Dict[str, Any]): State dict from a model.
   143→
   144→    Returns:
   145→        Set[str]: Set of keys in the state dict that correspond to LoRA modules.
   146→    """
   147→    lora_keys = [k for k in state_dict.keys() if "lora" in k or "magnitude" in k]
   148→    return set(
   149→        [
   150→            k.replace(".lora_a.weight", "")
   151→            .replace(".lora_b.weight", "")
   152→            .replace(".magnitude", "")
   153→            for k in lora_keys
   154→        ]
   155→    )

   158→@torch.no_grad
   159→def get_merged_lora_ckpt(
   160→    state_dict: Dict[str, Any],
   161→    rank: int,
   162→    alpha: float,
   163→) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   164→    """
   165→    Merge LoRA weights into the base model format for efficient inference.
   166→    NOTE: This function modifies state_dict inplace. If you do not want to do that,
   167→    make a copy prior to calling this function.
   168→
   169→    For every LoRA module in the state dict, this function will convert its
   170→    base weight then delete the LoRA-specific parameters.
   171→
   172→    Args:
   173→        state_dict (Dict[str, Any]): State dict from a model.
   174→        rank (int): The rank of LoRA matrices.
   175→        alpha (float): The alpha value used for scaling LoRA decompositions.
   176→
   177→    Returns:
   178→        Dict[str, Any]: The merged state dict.
   179→    """
   180→    lora_modules = _get_lora_modules(state_dict)
   181→    for module in lora_modules:
   182→        lora_a_weight = state_dict[f"{module}.lora_a.weight"]
   183→        lora_b_weight = state_dict[f"{module}.lora_b.weight"]
   184→        lora_magnitude = state_dict.get(f"{module}.magnitude", None)
   185→
   186→        # If magnitude is present, calculate merged DoRA weight
   187→        if lora_magnitude is not None:
   188→            base_weight = state_dict[f"{module}.weight"].to(lora_a_weight.dtype)
   189→
   190→            lora_weight = (alpha / rank) * lora_b_weight @ lora_a_weight
   191→            merged_weight = base_weight + lora_weight
   192→            weight_norm = torch.linalg.norm(base_weight + lora_weight, dim=1)
   193→            mag_norm_scale = (lora_magnitude / weight_norm).view(-1, 1)
   194→            merged_weight *= mag_norm_scale
   195→            state_dict[f"{module}.weight"] = merged_weight
   196→            del state_dict[f"{module}.magnitude"]
   197→
   198→        # Otherwise it is just vanilla LoRA
   199→        else:
   200→            state_dict[f"{module}.weight"] += (
   201→                (alpha / rank) * lora_b_weight @ lora_a_weight
   202→            )
   203→
   204→        del state_dict[f"{module}.lora_a.weight"]
   205→        del state_dict[f"{module}.lora_b.weight"]
   206→
   207→    return state_dict

   210→@contextlib.contextmanager
   211→def disable_adapter(model: nn.Module) -> Generator[None, None, None]:
   212→    """
   213→    Temporarily disable the adapters in a model. For example,
   214→    this can be used in DPO for treating the LoRA adapters as the policy model
   215→    and disabling it to treat the base model as the reference model.
   216→
   217→    This context manager goes through all modules in the provided neural network model,
   218→    and if a module has an ``adapter_params`` attribute that is callable and a ``disabled`` attribute,
   219→    it sets ``disabled`` to True. Then, the control is given back to caller. When exiting the context manager,
   220→    it sets ``disabled`` back to False for all modules that were temporarily disabled.
   221→
   222→    Args:
   223→        model (nn.Module): The model whose adapters are to be temporarily disabled.
   224→    Yields:
   225→        None: This function yields control back to the caller, with the adapters disabled.
   226→    Example:
   227→        >>> with disable_adapter(model):
   228→        ...     # Perform operations with adapters disabled
   229→        ...     pass
   230→
   231→    """
   232→    for _, module in model.named_modules():
   233→        if (
   234→            hasattr(module, "adapter_params")
   235→            and callable(module.adapter_params)
   236→            and hasattr(module, "disabled")
   237→        ):
   238→            module.disabled = True
   239→    try:
   240→        yield
   241→    finally:
   242→        for _, module in model.named_modules():
   243→            if (
   244→                hasattr(module, "adapter_params")
   245→                and callable(module.adapter_params)
   246→                and hasattr(module, "disabled")
   247→            ):
   248→                module.disabled = False

   251→def validate_missing_and_unexpected_for_lora(
   252→    lora_attn_modules: List[LORA_ATTN_MODULES],
   253→    apply_lora_to_mlp: bool,
   254→    apply_lora_to_output: bool,
   255→    base_missing: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   256→    base_unexpected: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   257→    lora_missing: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   258→    lora_unexpected: Optional[List[str]] = None,
   259→) -> None:
   260→    """
   261→    A more memory-efficient way to validate that LoRA state dict loading was done properly.
   262→
   263→    This function uses a model's LoRA config to check that LoRA and/or base model weights
   264→    are loaded into the full model correctly. This function relies only on the values of missing and
   265→    unexpected as returned by the load_state_dict API with strict=False. This allows us to do the
   266→    validation without any additional calls to .state_dict(), which use additional memory.
   267→
   268→    Args:
   269→        lora_attn_modules (List[LORA_ATTN_MODULES]): list of which linear layers
   270→            LoRA should be applied to in each self-attention block. Options are
   271→            ``{"q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "output_proj"}``.
   272→        apply_lora_to_mlp (bool): whether LoRA is applied to each MLP linear.
   273→        apply_lora_to_output (bool): whether LoRA is applied to the final output projection.
   274→        base_missing (Optional[List[str]]): List of missing keys when loading base model weights.
   275→            Default: None
   276→        base_unexpected (Optional[List[str]]): List of unexpected keys when loading base model weights.
   277→            Default: None
   278→        lora_missing (Optional[List[str]]): List of missing keys when loading LoRA weights.
   279→            Default: None
   280→        lora_unexpected (Optional[List[str]]): List of unexpected keys when loading LoRA weights.
   281→            Default: None
   282→
   283→    Returns:
   284→        None
   285→
   286→    Raises:
   287→        AssertionError: if base_missing contains any base model keys.
   288→        AssertionError: if base_unexpected is nonempty.
   289→        AssertionError: if lora_missing contains any LoRA keys.
   290→        AssertionError: if lora_unexpected is nonempty.
   291→    """
   292→    lora_modules = get_lora_module_names(
   293→        lora_attn_modules, apply_lora_to_mlp, apply_lora_to_output
   294→    )
   295→    is_lora_param = lambda x: any(
   296→        [
   297→            ".".join([k, "lora"]) in x or ".".join([k, "magnitude"]) in x
   298→            for k in lora_modules
   299→        ]
   300→    )
   301→
   302→    if base_missing:
   303→        for k in base_missing:
   304→            if not is_lora_param(k):
   305→                raise AssertionError(f"Missing non-LoRA key {k} from base model dict")
   306→    if base_unexpected:
   307→        raise AssertionError("Unexpected key loading base model")
   308→    if lora_missing:
   309→        for k in lora_missing:
   310→            if is_lora_param(k):
   311→                raise AssertionError(f"Missing LoRA key {k} from adapter state dict")
   312→    if lora_unexpected:
   313→        raise AssertionError("Unexpected key loading adapter")
   314→

   316→def load_dora_magnitudes(model: nn.Module) -> None:
   317→    """

   320→    dora_parents = {
   321→        n: p for n, p in model.named_modules() if hasattr(p, "adapter_params")

    42→class LoRAFinetuneRecipeSingleDevice(FTRecipeInterface):
    43→    """
    44→    LoRA finetuning recipe for dense transformer-based LLMs such as Llama2. This recipe is optimized
    45→    for single GPU training. Training on CPU is not supported.
    46→
    47→    Features:
    48→        - Activation Checkpointing. This can be controlled using the ``enable_activation_checkpointing``
    49→            flag. Activation checkpointing helps reduce the memory footprint since we no longer keep
    50→            activations in memory and instead recompute them during the backward pass. This is especially
    51→            helpful for larger batch sizes when you're memory constrained. But these savings in memory
    52→            come at the cost of training performance. In most cases training can slow-down quite a bit as
    53→            a result of this activation recomputation.
    54→
    55→        - Activation Offloading. This can be controlled using the ``enable_activation_offloading``
    56→            flag. Activation offloading is a technique similar to activations checkpointing that helps
    57→            reduce the memory footprint to prevent OOMs on CUDA and enable bigger batches. Where activations
    58→            checkpointing drops the activation in the forward to recompute it later in the backward,
    59→            activations offloading will drop the activation in the forward to the CPU and bring it
    60→            back during the backward pass. As always, there is a tradeoff--these savings in memory can
    61→            come at the cost of training performance and CPU resources. To recover some runtime cost,
    62→            we've added an option to enable offloading on a different stream to permit overlapping with
    63→            the computation. This option is currently only available on PyTorch 2.5 or later and will
    64→            be enabled by default if an acceptable torch version is found. Activation offloading can be
    65→            used in conjunction with activation checkpointing.
    66→
    67→        - Precision. Full fp32 and bf16 training are supported. Precision is controlled using the ``dtype``
    68→            flag. When ``dtype=bf16``, all activations, gradients and optimizer states are in bfloat16. In
    69→            most cases this should halve the memory footprint of full precision (fp32) training, without
    70→            loss in model quality (will depend on the model, training data and other settings). For
    71→            GPUs which do not support bfloat16, we fall back to fp32. Mixed precision training and fp16
    72→            precision are currently not supported.
    73→
    74→        - Gradient Accumulation. You can simulate larger batch sizes by accumulating gradients. This is
    75→            controlled using the ``gradient_accumulation_steps`` flag.
    76→
    77→                Total Batch Size = batch_size * gradient accumulation steps.
    78→
    79→            For example: with batch_size=1 and gradient_accumulation_steps=32 we get a total batch size of 32.
    80→
    81→            Gradient accumulation is especially useful when you are memory constrained. In this case,
    82→            accumulating gradients might give you better training speed than enabling activation
    83→            checkpointing.
    84→
    85→        - Lower precision optimizers. This recipe supports lower-precision optimizers from the bitsandbytes
    86→            library (https://huggingface.co/docs/bitsandbytes/main/en/index). We've tested the recipe with
    87→            8-bit AdamW and Paged AdamW.
    88→
    89→        - Checkpointing. Model weights are checkpointed both at the end of each epoch and at the end of
    90→            training. Currently we checkpoint both the adapter weights (trainable params only) and the
    91→            complete merged weights (adapter weights added back to the base model). For more details
    92→            please take a look at our LoRA tutorial
    93→            (https://pytorch.org/torchtune/main/tutorials/lora_finetune.html).
    94→
    95→            Optimizer State and recipe state (seed, total_epochs, number of epochs run etc) are
    96→            only saved at the end of a given epoch and used in case of resuming training. Resuming
    97→            training is controlled by the ``resume_from_checkpoint`` flag. Mid-epoch checkpointing is
    98→            currently not supported.
    99→
   100→            For more details on the checkpointer, please take a look at
   101→            our checkpointer deepdive (https://pytorch.org/torchtune/main/tutorials/checkpointer.html).
   102→
   103→        - Logging. Terminal, Disk, WandB and TensorBoard are all supported.
   104→
   105→        - Gradient Clipping. Gradient clipping is supported using the ``clip_grad_norm`` flag. By default,
   106→            ``clip_grad_norm`` is set to ``None``. If you only want to log the grad norm, you can set
   107→            ``clip_grad_norm='inf'``.
   108→
   109→    For a full list of example configs for this recipe, run ``tune ls`` on the command line. Each config
   110→    has example commands for how to kick-off training.
   111→
   112→    Args:
   113→        cfg (DictConfig): OmegaConf object parsed from yaml file
   114→
   115→    Raises:
   116→        ValueError: If ``dtype`` is set to fp16.
   117→        RuntimeError: If ``dtype`` is set to bf16 and the hardware does not support bf16.
   118→        RuntimeError: If ``enable_activation_offloading`` is True and device is not CUDA.
   119→        RuntimeError: If ``enable_activation_offloading`` is True and ``enable_activation_checkpointing`` is False.
   120→        RuntimeError: If ``left_pad_sequence`` is set as the data collator
   121→
   122→    """
   123→
   124→    def __init__(self, cfg: DictConfig) -> None:
   125→        self._device = utils.get_device(device=cfg.device)
   126→        # Reduced precision logic
   127→        self._dtype = training.get_dtype(cfg.dtype, device=self._device)
   128→        # fp16 precision is explicitly disabled as it is not supported in this
   129→        # recipe (for example, no gradient scaling).
   130→        if self._dtype == torch.float16:
   131→            raise ValueError(
   132→                "fp16 precision is not supported in this recipe. Please use fp32 or bf16."
   133→            )
   134→
   135→        # logging attributes
   136→        self._output_dir = cfg.output_dir
   137→        self._log_every_n_steps = cfg.get("log_every_n_steps", 1)
   138→        self._log_peak_memory_stats = cfg.get("log_peak_memory_stats", False)
   139→
   140→        if self._log_peak_memory_stats and self._device.type != "cuda":
   141→            log.info(
   142→                "log_peak_memory_stats was set to True, however, training does not use cuda. Setting log_peak_memory_stats=False."
   143→            )
   144→            self._log_peak_memory_stats = False
   145→
   146→        # These are public properties which are updated by the checkpoint loader
   147→        # when ``resume_from_checkpoint`` is `True` or validated in tests
   148→        self.seed = training.set_seed(seed=cfg.seed)
   149→        self.epochs_run = 0
   150→        self.total_epochs = cfg.epochs
   151→        self.max_steps_per_epoch = cfg.max_steps_per_epoch
   152→        self.global_step = 0
   153→        self._resume_from_checkpoint = cfg.resume_from_checkpoint
   154→        self._save_adapter_weights_only = cfg.get("save_adapter_weights_only", False)
   155→        self._gradient_accumulation_steps = cfg.gradient_accumulation_steps
   156→        self._clip_grad_norm = cfg.get("clip_grad_norm", None)
   157→
   158→        # activation checkpointing/offloading
   159→        self._enable_activation_checkpointing = cfg.get(
   160→            "enable_activation_checkpointing", False
   161→        )
   162→        self._enable_activation_offloading = cfg.get(
   163→            "enable_activation_offloading", False
   164→        )
   165→        if self._enable_activation_offloading:
   166→            if self._device.type != "cuda":
   167→                raise RuntimeError(
   168→                    "enable_activation_offloading should only be True when training on CUDA"
   169→                )
   170→            if not self._enable_activation_checkpointing:
   171→                raise RuntimeError(
   172→                    "enable_activation_offloading should only be True when enable_activation_checkpointing is True"
   173→                )
   174→        elif (
   175→            self._enable_activation_checkpointing
   176→            and cfg.checkpointer.model_type != "LLAMA3_VISION"
   177→        ):
   178→            utils.log_rank_zero(
   179→                log,
   180→                "Hint: enable_activation_checkpointing is True, but enable_activation_offloading isn't. "
   181→                "Enabling activation offloading should reduce memory further.",
   182→            )
   183→
   184→    def load_checkpoint(self, cfg_checkpointer: DictConfig) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   185→        """
   186→        Extract the checkpoint state from file and validate. This includes the
   187→        base model weights. If resume_from_checkpoint is True, this also includes
   188→        the adapter weights and recipe state
   189→        """
   190→        self._checkpointer = config.instantiate(
   191→            cfg_checkpointer,
   192→            resume_from_checkpoint=self._resume_from_checkpoint,
   193→        )
   194→        checkpoint_dict = self._checkpointer.load_checkpoint()
   195→
   196→        if self._resume_from_checkpoint:
   197→            if training.ADAPTER_KEY not in checkpoint_dict:
   198→                raise ValueError(
   199→                    "Adapter weights not found. Please ensure a valid adapter checkpoint is provided."
   200→                )
   201→            # _update_recipe_state will throw an exception if the recipe state is not corrctly loaded
   202→            # no need to check here
   203→            self._update_recipe_state(checkpoint_dict)
   204→        return checkpoint_dict
   205→
   206→    def _update_recipe_state(self, ckpt_dict: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   207→        """
   208→        Updates the recipe state from checkpoint.
   209→        """
   210→        try:
   211→            self.epochs_run = ckpt_dict[training.EPOCHS_KEY]
   212→
   213→            # on mismatch, warn the user and prevent the override
   214→            if self.seed != ckpt_dict[training.SEED_KEY]:
   215→                warn(
   216→                    message=(
   217→                        "Config value for seed does not match the checkpoint value, "
   218→                        f"using the checkpoint value: {ckpt_dict[training.SEED_KEY]}"
   219→                    )
   220→                )
   221→                self.seed = ckpt_dict[training.SEED_KEY]
   222→            if self.max_steps_per_epoch != ckpt_dict[training.MAX_STEPS_KEY]:
   223→                warn(
   224→                    message=(
   225→                        "Config value for max_steps_per_epoch does not match the checkpoint value, "
   226→                        f"using the checkpoint value: {ckpt_dict[training.MAX_STEPS_KEY]}"
   227→                    )
   228→                )
   229→                self.max_steps_per_epoch = ckpt_dict[training.MAX_STEPS_KEY]
   230→
   231→            # on mismatch, warn the user but allow the override
   232→            if self.total_epochs != ckpt_dict[training.TOTAL_EPOCHS_KEY]:
   233→                warn(
   234→                    message=(
   235→                        "Config value for total_epochs does not match the checkpoint value, "
   236→                        f"using the config value: {self.total_epochs}"
   237→                    )
   238→                )
   239→
   240→        except KeyError as e:
   241→            raise KeyError(
   242→                "Checkpoint does not contain the required keys needed for updating recipe state. "
   243→                "Are you sure you passed in the right recipe checkpoint?"
   244→            ) from e
   245→
   246→    def setup(self, cfg: DictConfig) -> None:
   247→        """
   248→        Setup the recipe state. This includes recipe state (if resume_from_checkpoint is True),
   249→        model, tokenizer, loss, optimizer, learning rate scheduler, sampler, and dataloader.
   250→        """
   251→        self._metric_logger = config.instantiate(cfg.metric_logger)
   252→
   253→        # log config with parameter override
   254→        self._metric_logger.log_config(cfg)
   255→
   256→        self._compile = cfg.compile
   257→        if cfg.device == "npu" and cfg.compile:
   258→            raise ValueError(
   259→                "NPU does not support model compilation. Please set `compile: False` in the config."
   260→            )
   261→        checkpoint_dict = self.load_checkpoint(cfg_checkpointer=cfg.checkpointer)
   262→
   263→        # hack to toggle to the low cpu ram version of the reparametrize_as_dtype
   264→        # hook based on the config.
   265→        common_utils._use_low_cpu_ram = cfg.get("low_cpu_ram", False)
   266→
   267→        # set up model
   268→        self._model = self._setup_model(
   269→            cfg_model=cfg.model,
   270→            enable_activation_checkpointing=self._enable_activation_checkpointing,
   271→            enable_activation_offloading=self._enable_activation_offloading,
   272→            compile_model=cfg.compile,
   273→            base_model_state_dict=checkpoint_dict[training.MODEL_KEY],
   274→            lora_weights_state_dict=(
   275→                checkpoint_dict[training.ADAPTER_KEY]
   276→                if self._resume_from_checkpoint
   277→                else None
   278→            ),
   279→        )
   280→
   281→        self._tokenizer = config.instantiate(cfg.tokenizer)
   282→        log.info("Tokenizer is initialized from file.")
   283→
   284→        self._optimizer = self._setup_optimizer(
   285→            cfg_optimizer=cfg.optimizer,
   286→            opt_state_dict=(
   287→                checkpoint_dict[training.OPT_KEY]
   288→                if self._resume_from_checkpoint
   289→                else None
   290→            ),
   291→        )
   292→
   293→        # initialize loss
   294→        self._loss_fn = config.instantiate(cfg.loss)
   295→        if self._compile:
   296→            self._loss_fn = training.compile_loss(self._loss_fn)
   297→
   298→        if self._loss_fn.__class__.__name__ == "CEWithChunkedOutputLoss":
   299→            # set num_output_chunks for model
   300→            self._model.set_num_output_chunks(self._loss_fn.num_output_chunks)
   301→
   302→        log.info("Loss is initialized.")
   303→
   304→        # Dataloader depends on the tokenizer and loss_fn and should be
   305→        # setup after all of these are setup
   306→        collate_name = cfg.get("collate_fn", "torchtune.data.padded_collate_sft")
   307→        self._sampler, self._dataloader = self._setup_data(
   308→            cfg_dataset=cfg.dataset,
   309→            shuffle=cfg.shuffle,
   310→            batch_size=cfg.batch_size,
   311→            collate_fn=collate_name,
   312→        )
   313→
   314        # Finally update the recipe state which can only be correctly set after all of the
   315→        # other components have been initialized and updated.
   316→
   317→        # Number of training steps in each epoch depends on the number of batches produced
   318→        # by the dataloader and the max_steps_per_epoch param set by the user and is used
   319→        # for logging and tracking training state. This should be computed after the dataloader
   320→        # has been setup
   321→        self._steps_per_epoch = (
   322→            len(self._dataloader) // self._gradient_accumulation_steps
   323→        )
   324→        if (
   325→            self.max_steps_per_epoch is not None
   326→            and self.max_steps_per_epoch < self._steps_per_epoch
   327→        ):
   328→            self._steps_per_epoch = self.max_steps_per_epoch
   329→            self.global_step = self.epochs_run * self._steps_per_epoch
   330→
   331→        # Learning rate scheduler can only be set up after number of steps
   332→        # has been computed
   333→        self._lr_scheduler = self._setup_lr_scheduler(
   334→            cfg_lr_scheduler=cfg.lr_scheduler,
   335→            num_training_steps=self.total_epochs * self._steps_per_epoch,
   336→            last_epoch=self.global_step - 1,
   337→        )
   338→
   339→        # Set up profiler, returns DummyProfiler (nullcontext object with no-op `step` method)
   340→        # if cfg is missing profiler key or if `cfg.profiler.enabled = False
   341→        self._profiler = self._setup_profiler(cfg.get(PROFILER_KEY, None))
   342→
   343→        # Used to ignore labels for loss computation
   344→        self.ignore_labels_cache = torch.full(
   345→            (cfg.batch_size, 1), self._loss_fn.ignore_index, device=self._device
   346→        )

   348→    def _setup_profiler(
   349→        self, cfg_profiler: Optional[DictConfig] = None
   350→    ) -> Union[torch.profiler.profile, DummyProfiler]:
   351→        """
   352→        Parses the `profiler` section of top-level `cfg` and sets up profiler
   353→
   354→        Args:
   355→            cfg_profiler (Optional[DictConfig]): ``profiler`` section of the top-level ``cfg`` (the main config passed to
   356→                `recipe.main`). Default None.
   357→
   358→        Returns:
   359→            profiler: Union[torch.profiler.profile, DummyProfiler] - DummyProfiler is a nullcontext with no-op methods
   360→            for `start`, `stop`, and `step` that can be used in place of `torch.profiler.profile` if profiler is not enabled such
   361→            that the instrumented training loop does not need to be changed profiling is disabled.
   362→
   363→        The profiler config can be provided in configs under the `profiler` key with the following layout:
   364→
   365→        .. code-block:: yaml
   366→            profiler:
   367→                enabled: bool
   368→
   369→                #Output directory of trace artifacts
   370→                output_dir: str
   371→
   372→            #`torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity` types to trace
   373→            cpu: bool
   374→            cuda: bool
   375→
   376→                #Trace options
   377→                profile_memory: bool
   378→                with_stack: bool
   379→                record_shapes: bool
   380→                with_flops: bool
   381→
   382→            # `torch.profiler.schedule` options:
   383→            # wait_steps -> wait, warmup_steps -> warmup, active_steps -> active, num_cycles -> repeat
   384→            wait_steps: int
   385→            warmup_steps: int
   386→            active_steps: int
   387→            num_cycles: int
   388→        """
   389→
   390→        # Missing profiler section in config, assume disabled
   391→        if cfg_profiler is None:
   392→            cfg_profiler = DictConfig({"enabled": False})
   393→
   394→        # Check that component is included and set correctly
   395→        if cfg_profiler.get("_component_", None) is None:
   396→            cfg_profiler["_component_"] = "torchtune.training.setup_torch_profiler"
   397→        else:
   398→            assert (
   399→                cfg_profiler.get("_component_")
   400→                == "torchtune.training.setup_torch_profiler"
   401→            ), "Only torch profiler supported currently: component must be `torchtune.training.setup_torch_profiler`"
   402→
   403→        profiler, profiler_cfg = config.instantiate(cfg_profiler)
   404→
   405→        log.info(f" Profiler config after instantiation: {profiler_cfg}")
   406→
   407→        self.profiler_profile_memory = profiler_cfg.get("profile_memory", False)
   408→        if profiler_cfg["enabled"]:
   409→            self.profiler_wait_steps = profiler_cfg["wait_steps"]
   410→            self.profiler_warmup_steps = profiler_cfg["warmup_steps"]
   411→            self.profiler_active_steps = profiler_cfg["active_steps"]
   412→
   413→        return profiler

   415→    def _setup_model(
   416→        self,
   417→        cfg_model: DictConfig,
   418→        enable_activation_checkpointing: bool,
   419→        enable_activation_offloading: bool,
   420→        compile_model: bool,
   421→        base_model_state_dict: Dict[str, Any],
   422→        lora_weights_state_dict: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   423→    ) -> nn.Module:
   424→        with training.set_default_dtype(self._dtype), self._device:
   425→            model = config.instantiate(cfg_model)
   426→
   427→        self._lora_rank = cfg_model.lora_rank
   428→        self._lora_alpha = cfg_model.lora_alpha
   429→        self._lora_attn_modules = list(cfg_model.lora_attn_modules)
   430→        self._apply_lora_to_mlp = cfg_model.apply_lora_to_mlp
   431→        self._apply_lora_to_output = getattr(cfg_model, "apply_lora_to_output", False)
   432→        self.adapter_params = get_adapter_params(model)
   433→        self._is_dora = any(["magnitude" in k for k in self.adapter_params.keys()])
   434→        set_trainable_params(model, self.adapter_params)
   435→
   436→        if compile_model:
   437→            training.compile_model(model)
   438→
   439→        if enable_activation_checkpointing:
   440→            training.set_activation_checkpointing(
   441→                model, auto_wrap_policy={modules.TransformerSelfAttentionLayer}
   442→            )
   443→
   444→        base_missing, base_unexpected = model.load_state_dict(
   445→            base_model_state_dict, strict=False
   446→        )
   447→        # This is for any adapters that need to be initialized after base weights
   448→        # have been loaded (e.g. DoRA).
   449→        if self._is_dora:
   450→            for m in model.modules():
   451→                if hasattr(m, "initialize_dora_magnitude"):
   452→                    m.initialize_dora_magnitude()
   453→            load_dora_magnitudes(model)
   454→        if lora_weights_state_dict:
   455→            lora_missing, lora_unexpected = model.load_state_dict(
   456→                lora_weights_state_dict, strict=False
   457→            )
   458→        else:
   459→            lora_missing, lora_unexpected = None, None
   460→
   461→        validate_missing_and_unexpected_for_lora(
   462→            lora_attn_modules=self._lora_attn_modules,
   463→            apply_lora_to_mlp=self._apply_lora_to_mlp,
   464→            apply_lora_to_output=self._apply_lora_to_output,
   465→            base_missing=base_missing,
   466→            base_unexpected=base_unexpected,
   467→            lora_missing=lora_missing,
   468→            lora_unexpected=lora_unexpected,
   469→        )
   470→        # Validate model adapter params were loaded in with the expected dtype
   471→        # TODO (rohan-varma): Further validation to ensure the appropriate base params
   472→        # are NF4 vs bf16 based on the quantization config.
   473→        training.validate_expected_param_dtype(
   474→            self.adapter_params.items(), dtype=self._dtype
   475→        )
   476→
   477→        # activation offloading
   478→        self.activations_handling_ctx = training.get_act_offloading_ctx_manager(
   479→            model, enable_activation_offloading
   480→        )
   481→
   482→        log.info(f"Model is initialized with precision {self._dtype}.")
   483→
   484→        if self._device.type != "cpu":
   485→            memory_stats = training.get_memory_stats(device=self._device)
   486→            training.log_memory_stats(memory_stats)
   487→        return model

   515→    def _setup_data(
   516→        self,
   517→        cfg_dataset: DictConfig,
   518→        shuffle: bool,
   519→        batch_size: int,
   520→        collate_fn: str,
   521→    ) -> Tuple[DistributedSampler, DataLoader]:
   522→        """
   523→        All data related setup happens here. Currently this recipe only supports
   524→        Map-style Datasets which fit into memory and an option for random shuffling.
   525→        Samplers, iterable datasets, and streaming datasets are not supported.
   526→        """
   527→        if isinstance(cfg_dataset, ListConfig):
   528→            datasets = [
   529→                config.instantiate(single_cfg_dataset, self._tokenizer)
   530→                for single_cfg_dataset in cfg_dataset
   531→            ]
   532→            ds = ConcatDataset(datasets=datasets)
   533→            packed = False
   534→        else:
   535→            ds = config.instantiate(cfg_dataset, self._tokenizer)
   536→            packed = cfg_dataset.get("packed", False)
   537→
   538→        # Instantiate collate_fn
   539→        if "left_pad_sequence" in collate_fn:
   540→            raise RuntimeError("left_pad_sequence collator is only for inference.")
   541→        collate_fn = _get_component_from_path(collate_fn)
   542→
   543→        sampler = DistributedSampler(
   544→            ds,
   545→            num_replicas=1,
   546→            rank=0,
   547→            shuffle=shuffle,
   548→            seed=0,
   549→        )
   550→        dataloader = DataLoader(
   551→            dataset=ds,
   552→            sampler=sampler,
   553→            batch_size=batch_size,
   554→            # dropping last avoids shape issues with compile + flex attention
   555→            drop_last=True,
   556→            collate_fn=(
   557→                partial(
   558                    collate_fn,
   559→                    padding_idx=self._tokenizer.pad_id,
   560→                    ignore_idx=self._loss_fn.ignore_index,
   561→                )
   562→                if not packed
   563→                else padded_collate_packed
   564→            ),
   565→        )
   566→
   567→        log.info("Dataset and Sampler are initialized.")
   568→
   569→        return sampler, dataloader

   571→    def save_checkpoint(self, epoch: int) -> None:
   572→        """
   573→        Checkpoint the state of the recipe. The constructed checkpoint state dict
   574→        contains the following information:
   575→        - Merged weights with key MODEL_KEY
   576→        - Adapter weights with key ADAPTER_KEY
   577→        - Relevant recipe state if training is not complete
   578→        - If the `self._save_adapter_weights_only` option is True, the checkpointer will save only the adapter weights
   579→
   580→        To correctly resume from training, the adapter weights and recipe state must be provided along with the base model weights.
   581→        """
   582→        ckpt_dict = {}
   583→
   584→        intermediate_checkpoint = epoch + 1 < self.total_epochs
   585→        # if training is in-progress, checkpoint the optimizer state as well
   586→        if intermediate_checkpoint:
   587→            ckpt_dict.update(
   588→                {
   589→                    training.OPT_KEY: self._optimizer.state_dict(),
   590→                    training.SEED_KEY: self.seed,
   591→                    training.EPOCHS_KEY: self.epochs_run,
   592→                    training.TOTAL_EPOCHS_KEY: self.total_epochs,
   593→                    training.MAX_STEPS_KEY: self.max_steps_per_epoch,
   594→                }
   595→            )
   596→
   597→        adapter_state_dict = get_adapter_state_dict(self._model.state_dict())
   598→        ckpt_dict.update({training.ADAPTER_KEY: adapter_state_dict})
   599→
   600→        if not self._save_adapter_weights_only:
   601→            # Construct the full state dict with LoRA weights merged into base LLM weights
   602→
   603→            # Move to CPU to avoid a copy on GPU
   604→            state_dict = {k: v.cpu() for k, v in self._model.state_dict().items()}
   605→
   606→            merged_state_dict = get_merged_lora_ckpt(
   607→                state_dict,
   608→                rank=self._lora_rank,
   609→                alpha=self._lora_alpha,
   610→            )
   611→
   612→            ckpt_dict.update({training.MODEL_KEY: merged_state_dict})
   613→
   614→        adapter_config = {
   615→            "r": self._lora_rank,
   616→            "lora_alpha": self._lora_alpha,
   617→            "target_modules": get_lora_module_names(
   618→                self._lora_attn_modules,
   619→                self._apply_lora_to_mlp,
   620→                self._apply_lora_to_output,
   621→            ),
   622→            "peft_type": "LORA",
   623→        }
   624→        ckpt_dict.update({training.ADAPTER_CONFIG: adapter_config})

   626→        self._checkpointer.save_checkpoint(
   627→            ckpt_dict,
   628→            epoch=epoch,
   629→            intermediate_checkpoint=intermediate_checkpoint,

   633→    def _loss_step(self, batch: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
   634→        # Shape [b, s], needed for the loss not the model
   635→        labels = batch.pop("labels")
   636→        # run model
   637→        with self.activations_handling_ctx:
   638→            logits = self._model(**batch)
   639→
   640→        # Shift labels to compute loss
   641→        # equivalent to doing labels[..., 1:] and logits[..., :-1, :]
   642→        # But this way we dont need to slice the logits. We just add an ignore index to labels.
   643→        labels = torch.hstack(
   644→            (labels[..., 1:], self.ignore_labels_cache[: labels.shape[0]])
   645→        )
   646→        if not isinstance(logits, list):
   647→            labels = labels.reshape(-1)
   648→            logits = logits.reshape(-1, logits.size(-1))
   649→
   650→        loss = self._loss_fn(logits, labels)
   651→
   652→        # free logits otherwise it peaks backward memory
   653→        del logits
   654→
   655→        return loss

   657→    def train(self) -> None:
   658→        """
   659→        The core training loop.
   660→        """
   661→
   662→        if self._compile:
   663→            log.info(
   664→                "NOTE: torch.compile is enabled and model is compiled in first forward. Expect a relatively slow first iteration."
   665→            )
   666→
   667→        # Initialize tokens count and running loss (for grad accumulation)
   668→        t0 = time.perf_counter()
   669→        running_loss = 0
   670→        num_tokens = 0
   671→
   672→        with self._profiler as prof:
   673→            # self.epochs_run should be non-zero when we're resuming from a checkpoint
   674→            for curr_epoch in range(self.epochs_run, self.total_epochs):
   675→                # Update the sampler to ensure data is correctly shuffled across epochs
   676→                # in case shuffle is True
   677→                self._sampler.set_epoch(curr_epoch)
   678→
   679→                pbar = tqdm(total=self._steps_per_epoch)
   680→                for idx, batch in enumerate(self._dataloader):
   681→                    if (
   682→                        self.max_steps_per_epoch is not None
   683→                        and (idx // self._gradient_accumulation_steps)
   684→                        == self.max_steps_per_epoch
   685→                    ):
   686→                        break
   687→
   688→                    # Start tracking CUDA memory for active steps for just the first epoch
   689→                    if (
   690→                        curr_epoch == 0
   691→                        and self.profiler_profile_memory
   692→                        and idx == self.profiler_wait_steps + self.profiler_warmup_steps
   693→                    ):
   694→                        torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history()
   695→
   696→                    utils.batch_to_device(batch, self._device)
   697→
   698→                    # Calculate the number of unmasked tokens in the current batch
   699→                    # and increment the total number of tokens seen in the step
   700→                    current_num_tokens = (
   701→                        batch["labels"] != self._loss_fn.ignore_index
   702→                    ).sum()
   703→                    num_tokens += current_num_tokens
   704→
   705→                    # Loss is normalized by default so we multiply by the number of tokens
   706→                    # This way we can normalize by the total number of tokens if we're accumulating gradients
   707→                    current_loss = self._loss_step(batch) * current_num_tokens
   708→                    running_loss += current_loss
   709→                    current_loss.backward()
   710→
   711→                    # Step with optimizer
   712→                    if (idx + 1) % self._gradient_accumulation_steps == 0:
   713→                        training.scale_grads(self._model, 1 / num_tokens)
   714→                        if self._clip_grad_norm is not None:
   715→                            grad_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
   716→                                self._model.parameters(),
   717→                                max_norm=float(self._clip_grad_norm),
   718→                            )
   719→                        self._optimizer.step()
   720→                        self._optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
   721→                        self._lr_scheduler.step()
   722→                        # Update the number of steps when the weights are updated
   723→                        self.global_step += 1
   724→
   725→                        loss_to_log = running_loss.item() / num_tokens
   726→                        pbar.update(1)
   727→                        pbar.set_description(
   728→                            f"{curr_epoch + 1}|{self.global_step}|Loss: {loss_to_log}"
   729→                        )
   730→
   731→                        # Log per-step metrics
   732→                        if self.global_step % self._log_every_n_steps == 0:
   733→                            time_per_step = time.perf_counter() - t0
   734→                            log_dict = {
   735→                                "loss": loss_to_log,
   736→                                "lr": self._optimizer.param_groups[0]["lr"],
   737→                                "tokens_per_second_per_gpu": num_tokens / time_per_step,
   738→                            }
   739→                            if (
   740→                                self._device.type == "cuda"
   741→                                and self._log_peak_memory_stats
   742→                            ):
   743→                                log_dict.update(
   744→                                    training.get_memory_stats(device=self._device)
   745→                                )
   746→                            if self._clip_grad_norm is not None:
   747→                                log_dict.update({"grad_norm": grad_norm})
   748→                            self._metric_logger.log_dict(
   749→                                log_dict,
   750→                                step=self.global_step,
   751→                            )
   752→
   753→                        # Reset running stats for the next step
   754→                        running_loss = 0
   755→                        num_tokens = 0
   756→                        t0 = time.perf_counter()
   757→
   758→                    # Stop tracking CUDA memory now that active steps are complete
   759→                    if (
   760→                        curr_epoch == 0
   761→                        and self.profiler_profile_memory
   762→                        and idx
   763→                        == self.profiler_wait_steps
   764→                        + self.profiler_warmup_steps
   765→                        + self.profiler_active_steps
   766→                    ):
   767→                        torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history(enabled=None)
   768→
   769→                    # Step the profiler
   770→                    # Note we are stepping each batch, which might not include optimizer step in the trace
   771→                    # if the schedule cycle doesn't align with gradient accumulation.
   772→                    prof.step()

   774→                self.epochs_run += 1
   775→                start_save_checkpoint = time.perf_counter()

   779→                    "Checkpoint saved in {:.2f} seconds.".format(
   780→                        time.perf_counter() - start_save_checkpoint

   150→def load_from_full_model_state_dict(
   151→    model: "FSDPModule",  # noqa
   152→    full_sd: Dict[str, Any],
   153→    device: torch.device,
   154→    is_rank_zero: bool,
   155→    strict: bool = False,
   156→    cpu_offload: bool = False,
   157→):
   158→    """
   159→    Converting full state dict into a sharded state dict
   160→    and loading it into FSDP model
   161→    - 'full' means plain tensor
   162→    - 'sharded' means `DTensor` where reach rank has a shard of the plain tensor
   163→    - `is_rank_zero` matters if only rank 0 pass in non-empty `full_sd` and
   164→       we need to broadcast from rank 0
   165→    """
   166→    meta_sharded_sd = model.state_dict()
   167→    sharded_sd = {}
   168→    for param_name, full_tensor in full_sd.items():
   169→        sharded_meta_param = meta_sharded_sd.get(param_name)
   170→        full_tensor = full_tensor.to(sharded_meta_param.dtype).to(device)
   171→        if hasattr(sharded_meta_param, "_local_tensor") and isinstance(
   172→            sharded_meta_param._local_tensor, NF4Tensor
   173→        ):
   174→            block_size = sharded_meta_param._local_tensor.block_size
   175→            scaler_block_size = sharded_meta_param._local_tensor.scaler_block_size
   176→            full_tensor = to_nf4(
   177→                full_tensor, block_size=block_size, scaler_block_size=scaler_block_size
   178→            )
   179→            # replicating logic from `_fsdp_param.py`` `_init_sharded_param`
   180→            # otherwise `distribute_tensor(DTensor(local=NF4))`
   181→            # requires dispatching `c10d.scatter_``
   182→            # long-term solution is `swap_tensor`
   183→            mesh = sharded_meta_param.device_mesh
   184→            if mesh.ndim > 1:
   185→                raise NotImplementedError(f"only support 1D FSDP but got {mesh.ndim=}")
   186→            shard_mesh_dim = 0
   187→            shard_world_size = mesh.size(shard_mesh_dim)
   188→            shard_rank = cast(
   189→                torch.distributed.ProcessGroup, mesh.get_group(shard_mesh_dim)
   190→            ).rank()
   191→            chunk = list(torch.chunk(full_tensor, shard_world_size, dim=0))[shard_rank]
   192→            sharded_param = full_tensor.new_zeros(chunk.size())
   193→            sharded_param[: chunk.size(0)].copy_(chunk)
   194→
   195→            # TODO: change to from_local API (need to add view support for NF4)
   196→            sharded_tensor = DTensor(
   197→                local_tensor=sharded_param,
   198→                spec=DTensorSpec(
   199→                    mesh=sharded_meta_param.device_mesh,
   200→                    placements=sharded_meta_param.placements,
   201→                    tensor_meta=TensorMeta(
   202→                        shape=sharded_meta_param.size(),
   203→                        dtype=sharded_meta_param.dtype,
   204→                        stride=sharded_meta_param.stride(),
   205→                    ),
   206→                ),
   207→                requires_grad=sharded_meta_param.requires_grad,
   208→            )
   209→
   210→        elif not hasattr(sharded_meta_param, "device_mesh"):
   211→            # In cases where parts of the model aren't sharded, some parameters will be plain tensors
   212→            sharded_tensor = full_tensor
   213→        else:
   214→            sharded_tensor = distribute_tensor(
   215→                full_tensor,
   216→                sharded_meta_param.device_mesh,
   217→                sharded_meta_param.placements,
   218→            )
   219→        if cpu_offload:
   220→            sharded_tensor = sharded_tensor.cpu()
   221→        sharded_sd[param_name] = nn.Parameter(sharded_tensor)
   222→    # choose `assign=True` since we cannot call `copy_` on meta tensor
   223→    return model.load_state_dict(sharded_sd, strict=strict, assign=True)

   226→def _gather_nf4_tensor(sharded_param: nn.Parameter) -> nn.Parameter:
   227→    """
   228→    Manually gather NF4Tensor parameter since it does not support all_gather
   229→    """
   230→    mesh = sharded_param.device_mesh
   231→    nf4_tensor = sharded_param._local_tensor
   232→    quant_params, metadata = nf4_tensor.fsdp_pre_all_gather(mesh)
   233→    full_quant_params = []
   234→    for quant_param in quant_params:
   235→        d0, *dn = quant_param.shape
   236→        shape = (d0 * mesh.get_group().size(), *dn)
   237→        full_quant_param = torch.empty(
   238→            shape, device=quant_param.device, dtype=quant_param.dtype
   239→        )
   240→        dist.all_gather_into_tensor(
   241→            full_quant_param, quant_param, mesh.get_group(), async_op=False
   242→        )
   243→        full_quant_params.append(full_quant_param)
   244→    full_param, _ = nf4_tensor.fsdp_post_all_gather(
   245→        full_quant_params, metadata, nf4_tensor.dtype
   246→    )
   247→    return full_param

   250→def gather_cpu_state_dict(
   251→    sharded_sd: Dict[str, DTensor],  # noqa
   252→    is_rank_zero: bool,
   253→    device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
   254→) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   255→    """
   256→    Converting sharded state dict into a full state dict on CPU
   257→    Returning non-empty result only on rank0 to avoid peaking CPU memory
   258→
   259→    Args:
   260→        sharded_sd (Dict[str, DTensor]): Sharded state dict of DTensors
   261→        is_rank_zero (bool): flag to check if the process is on rank 0
   262→        device (Optional[torch.device]): device to use for sharded tensors. Default: None
   263→
   264→    Returns:
   265→        Dict[str, Any]: State dict on CPU
   266→    """
   267→    cpu_state_dict = {}
   268→    for param_name, param in sharded_sd.items():
   269→        if param.is_cpu:
   270→            # Move back to device if offloaded to CPU
   271→            param = param.to(device)
   272→        if hasattr(param, "_local_tensor"):
   273→            if isinstance(param._local_tensor, NF4Tensor):
   274→                param = _gather_nf4_tensor(param)
   275→            else:
   276→                # Gather DTensor
   277→                param = param.full_tensor()
   278→        if isinstance(param, NF4Tensor):
   279→            # upcasting NF4 to original dtype
   280→            param = param.to(param.dtype)
   281→        if is_rank_zero:
   282→            cpu_state_dict[param_name] = param.cpu()
   283→        torch.distributed.barrier()
   284→    return cpu_state_dict

   287→def get_full_optimizer_state_dict(
   288→    opt: Optimizer,
   289→    is_rank_zero: bool,
   290→    device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
   291→) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   292→    """
   293→    Converting optimizer state from sharded to full
   294→    For example, "exp_avg" in AdamW is `DTensor`,
   295→    "exp_avg.full_tensor()" converts it to plain tensor on rank 0
   296→    Returning non-empty cpu state dict on rank 0
   297→    """
   298→    sharded_sd = opt.state_dict()
   299→    sharded_state = sharded_sd["state"]
   300→    full_state = {}
   301→    for group_id, sharded_group in sharded_state.items():
   302→        group_state = {}
   303→        for attr, sharded_tensor in sharded_group.items():
   304→            # without this, it may hang forever for +70B models.
   305→            torch.distributed.barrier()
   306→            # "exp_avg" in AdamW is `DTensor`
   307→            if isinstance(sharded_tensor, DTensor):
   308→                if sharded_tensor.is_cpu:
   309→                    assert device is not None and device.type == "cuda", (
   310→                        f"Expect cuda but got device={device}. "
   311→                        "Please call get_full_optimizer_state_dict(..., device=self._device),"
   312→                        " so DTensor can communicate over NCCL."
   313→                    )
   314→                    sharded_tensor = sharded_tensor.to(device)
